'''Northwest Gas Pipeline''' is an operating natural gas pipeline in the northwestern United States. <ref name = source1> [http://co.williams.com/operations-2/west-operations/northwest-pipeline/ "Northwest Pipeline"] Williams Companies January 2018 </ref>

==Location==
The pipeline runs bidirectionally from Sumas, Washington, to La Plata County, Colorado.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://rextag.com/pages/northwest-pipeline?srsltid=AfmBOoocqYCYH-GTN35CdUx3Cod1eDFRxZtnQw6nC57500iLfiLQzW9G|title=Northwest Pipeline|website=Rextag Corporation Store|language=en|access-date=2025-09-20}}</ref>

==Background==

=== Main Line ===
The Northwest Pipeline system is a primary artery for the transmission of natural gas to the Pacific Northwest and Intermountain Region. It began as a 1,500-mile pipeline and has since expanded into a 3,900-mile bi-directional transmission system crossing the states of Washington, Oregon, Idaho, Wyoming, Utah and Colorado. Northwest’s bi-directional system provides access to British Columbia, Alberta, Rocky Mountain and San Juan Basin gas supplies. <ref name="source1"> [http://co.williams.com/operations-2/west-operations/northwest-pipeline/ "Northwest Pipeline"] Williams Companies January 2018 </ref> 

=== Trail West/N-Max ===
The Trail West/N-Max project would deliver more gas to the Portland area from a major existing pipeline in Central Oregon. The new 30-inch diameter gas pipeline was designed to transport 450 million cubic feet per day with an option to double that amount in the future. The industry believed that it could go into service by late 2023.<ref name="s13">Eric De Place, [https://www.sightline.org/2019/06/06/gas-industry-pnw-threats-despite-jay-inslee-opposition/ Despite Inslee’s Opposition, Gas Industry Still Plans Big Expansion in the PNW], Sightline Institute, June 6, 2019</ref>

According to the July 2023 update of the EIA database the project status is on-hold/cancelled.<ref name="eia" />

=== Kalama Lateral Project ===
The Kalama Lateral Project was proposed in 2016 to transport natural gas to a proposed Northwest Innovation Works methanol plant in Washington, United States.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.spglobal.com/marketintelligence/en/news-insights/latest-news-headlines/northwest-pipeline-gets-2-more-years-to-put-gas-lateral-in-service-58333711|title=Northwest Pipeline gets 2 more years to put gas lateral in service|website=www.spglobal.com|language=en-us|access-date=2022-12-07}}</ref> FERC issued extensions to Northwest Pipeline Co in 2018 and 2019, and in April 2022 it granted a third extension to the required in-service date out to April 2022. The methanol plant was cancelled in 2021, effectively cancelling the lateral project despite the permit extension.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oilandgaswatch.org/pipeline/3307|title=EIP Oil & Gas Watch|website=oilandgaswatch.org|language=en|access-date=2025-09-20}}</ref>

=== Kelso-Beaver Reliability Project ===
The proposed Kelso Beaver Reliability Project aims provide a total of approximately 183,000 dekatherms per day (Dth/d) of pipeline capacity to the Northwest Pipeline system by the third quarter of 2028. The project involves acquiring the existing 18-mile KB pipeline and installing a new compressor station. The project does not involve new pipeline construction.<ref name="eia" /><ref name=":2" />

=== Wild Trail Project ===
The proposed Wild Trail project will increase transportation capacity within the existing Northwest Pipeline system, moving resources from the Wild Horse Receipt Point to the Kern River Muddy Creek and Ignacio Delivery Points. The project includes a new compressor station, adjacent to the existing Northwest Pipeline Clay Basin Meter Station. No new pipelines are proposed in this project. The project will add 57,955 Dth/d plus contract for another 25,000 dth/d for a total project capacity of 82,955 Dth/d.<ref name="eia" />
